claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering can be used to produce consolidated refractory high-entropy alloys.
A mechanically alloyed RHEA-Cu powder mixture tends to segregate during conventional processing.
A large positive heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu drives phase segregation.
High SPS heating rates and controlled high pressure can kinetically trap a metastable phase in an RHEA-Cu composite.
Kinetic trapping during SPS can overcome the effects of the positive heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu.
High heating rates and applied pressure accelerate reaction kinetics and leave insufficient time for equilibrium phase segregation.
SPS processing can produce a fine-grained RHEA matrix.
SPS will homogenize the phase distribution of an RHEA-Cu composite.
The metastable RHEA-Cu microstructure will bypass equilibrium segregation.
The optimized SPS route will yield a stable RHEA-Cu microstructure on a large scale.
Compared with conventional sintering, optimized SPS will reduce phase segregation and refine grains.
Compared with conventional sintering, optimized SPS will improve the mechanical properties of the RHEA-Cu composite.
Conventional sintering or static powder processing typically causes phase segregation and unstable microstructures because of slow diffusion kinetics.
A protective or controlled atmosphere can be used during mechanical-alloying and SPS processing of an RHEA.
The proposed high-temperature controlled-atmosphere processing conditions mimic nuclear-reactor cooling conditions.
Undesired oxide or carbide phases can form during mechanically alloyed and SPS-consolidated RHEA processing, even when a protective atmosphere is used.
Excessive SPS heating rate or pressure specifically causes oxide formation or over-sintering.
The optimal SPS heating-rate and pressure window for suppressing segregation across different RHEA-Cu compositions and scales is unknown.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and conditions state that the method yields a stable microstructure on a large scale and ensures scale-up feasibility, whereas the boundary and uncertainty fields say scalability across larger volumes and compositions remains to be validated.
